You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 8fc9a77bc64e1f23d07953439817d8402ac9706f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sergey Shtylyov <s.shtylyov@omp.ru>
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2021 23:27:17 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] mmc: meson-mx-sdio: add IRQ check

The driver neglects to check the result of platform_get_irq()'s call and
blithely passes the negative error codes to devm_request_threaded_irq()
(which takes *unsigned* IRQ #), causing it to fail with -EINVAL, overriding
an original error code. Stop calling devm_request_threaded_irq() with the
invalid IRQ #s.

Fixes: ed80a13bb4c4 ("mmc: meson-mx-sdio: Add a driver for the Amlogic Meson8 and Meson8b SoC")
Signed-off-by: Sergey Shtylyov <s.shtylyov@omp.ru>
Reviewed-by: Martin Blumenstingl <martin.blumenstingl@googlemail.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211217202717.10041-3-s.shtylyov@omp.ru
Signed-off-by: Ulf Hansson <ulf.hansson@linaro.org>
---
 drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c | 5 +++++
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+)

diff --git a/drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c b/drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c
index d4a48916bfb6..3a19a05ef55a 100644
--- a/drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c
+++ b/drivers/mmc/host/meson-mx-sdio.c
@@ -662,6 +662,11 @@ static int meson_mx_mmc_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 	}
 
 	irq = platform_get_irq(pdev, 0);
+	if (irq < 0) {
+		ret = irq;
+		goto error_free_mmc;
+	}
+
 	ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(host->controller_dev, irq,
 					meson_mx_mmc_irq,
 					meson_mx_mmc_irq_thread, IRQF_ONESHOT,
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the driver not checking the return value of the `platform_get_irq()` function, which can return a negative error code if it fails to retrieve a valid IRQ number. This negative error code was being passed directly to `devm_request_threaded_irq()`, which expects an unsigned IRQ number, leading to an invalid IRQ number being used and causing the function to fail with an `-EINVAL` error. The patch adds a check for the return value of `platform_get_irq()` to handle this case properly.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by the driver not checking the return value of the `platform_get_irq()` function, which can return a negative error code if it fails to retrieve a valid IRQ number. This negative error code was being passed directly to `devm_request_threaded_irq()`, which expects an unsigned IRQ number, leading to an invalid IRQ number being used and causing the function to fail with an `-EINVAL` error. The patch adds a check for the return value of `platform_get_irq()` to handle this case properly.
